title: Stalkwise integral sections of a quasi-coherent algebra on a scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal B$ a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras whose underlying Zariski module is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. For every open $V\subseteq Y$, define $\mathcal D(V)=\{b\in\mathcal B(V): b_y\text{ is integral over }\mathcal O_{Y,y}\text{ for every }y\in V\}$, where $b_y$ is the germ in the module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and integral means satisfying a monic polynomial under the stalk structure map [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. With the restrictions inherited from $\mathcal B$, this is a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_Y$-subalgebra. For each $y\in Y$, the inclusion identifies $\mathcal D_y$ with the integral closure of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ in $\mathcal B_y$. For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, its sections $\mathcal D(V)\subseteq\mathcal B(V)$ are the integral closure of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$ in $\mathcal B(V)$. No reducedness, Noetherian, separation, finite-type, or nonemptiness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Restriction preserves the condition defining $\mathcal D$, because the germ of a restriction at a point is the same germ. Compatible sections in $\mathcal D(V_i)$ glue uniquely in $\mathcal B(V)$, and the glued germ at $y\in V_i$ is the given integral germ; hence the glued section lies in $\mathcal D(V)$. In each stalk, the integral elements form a subring containing the image of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Thus addition, negation, multiplication, the unit, and multiplication by a section of $\mathcal O_Y$ preserve the condition pointwise. This makes $\mathcal D$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-subalgebra sheaf of $\mathcal B$.

Fix any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and put $A=\mathcal B(V)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) to the underlying quasi-coherent module: its restriction to $V$ is canonically $\widetilde A$. The principal-open and stalk calculations [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identify sections on $D(f)$ with $A_f$ and the germ map at $\mathfrak p$ with $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$, over $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$. These are algebra identifications: products of fractions are $a/f^i\cdot b/f^j=ab/f^{i+j}$, and germ maps preserve multiplication. Consequently the condition $a\in\mathcal D(V)$ says precisely that $a/1$ is integral over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ for every $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-sfb-integral-element-prime-local-criterion], this is equivalent to $a$ being integral over $R$. Thus $\mathcal D(V)=C$, the integral closure of $R$ in $A$.

For the same affine $V$ and any $f\in R$, step 2 applied to the affine $D(f)$ identifies $\mathcal D(D(f))$ with the integral closure of $R_f$ in $A_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], this is $C_f$ as a submodule of $A_f$, and restriction sends $c$ to $c/1$. In particular every section on $D(f)$ is $c/f^n$, so multiplying it by $f^n$ extends to $c\in\mathcal D(V)$; if $c\in C$ restricts to zero, the fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $f^n c=0$ for some $n$. These are the two hypotheses of [pqf-lem-qcoh-principal-open-criterion], on every affine open. That criterion proves that the underlying module of $\mathcal D$ is quasi-coherent; by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] this is the required quasi-coherent algebra.

Fix $y\in V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, corresponding to $\mathfrak p$. The map $\mathcal D_y\to\mathcal B_y$ is injective: equality of the two image germs means their representatives agree on a common neighbourhood in $\mathcal B$, hence in the subsheaf $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Its image consists of integral germs by the definition of $\mathcal D$. Conversely identify $\mathcal B_y=A_{\mathfrak p}$ by the affine module and stalk calculations cited in step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], any element integral over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $c/s$ for $c\in C$ and $s\notin\mathfrak p$. Step 2 gives $c\in\mathcal D(V)$. On $D(s)$ the section $s$ of the structure sheaf is invertible, so the subalgebra property in step 1 gives $s^{-1}c\in\mathcal D(D(s))$ with the prescribed germ. Thus the image is exactly the integral closure, as an algebra over $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. This argument is local to one affine neighbourhood and uses no separation or finiteness hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem exists_quasiCoherent_stalkwiseIntegralClosure (Y : Scheme.{u}) (B : Y.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hB : Y.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra B) : ∃ (D : Y.CommAlgebraSheaf) (ι : D ⟶ B), Y.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra D ∧ (∀ V : Y.Opens, Function.Injective (ι.right.hom.app (op V))) ∧ (∀ (V : Y.Opens) (b : B.right.obj.obj (op V)), b ∈ Set.range (ι.right.hom.app (op V)) ↔ ∀ (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ V), ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).map B.hom.hom).hom.IsIntegralElem (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := CommRingCat) B.right.obj V y hy b)) ∧ (∀ y : Y, Function.Injective ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).map ι.right.hom) ∧ ∀ b : (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).obj B.right.obj, b ∈ Set.range ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).map ι.right.hom) ↔ ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).map B.hom.hom).hom.IsIntegralElem b) ∧ (∀ (V : Y.Opens), IsAffineOpen V → ∀ b : B.right.obj.obj (op V), b ∈ Set.range (ι.right.hom.app (op V)) ↔ (B.hom.hom.app (op V)).hom.IsIntegralElem b)
